trajectory.patch:
Based on the error log, the Kconfig options `MAX_THREAD_BYTES` and `BOUNDS_CHECK_BYPASS_MITIGATION` are being set in `tests/kernel/common/prj.conf`, but their dependencies are not met because `USERSPACE` is not enabled for the target platform. This happens when running the test suite on a board that does not support userspace.

The `BOUNDS_CHECK_BYPASS_MITIGATION` option is defined within an `if USERSPACE` block in `kernel/userspace/Kconfig`, making it unavailable when `USERSPACE` is disabled. However, the C code that implements this feature is already conditionally compiled based on `CONFIG_USERSPACE`. Therefore, it is safe to make the Kconfig option independent of `USERSPACE`. This will resolve the warning by making the option always visible, while its effect will remain conditional on `USERSPACE` being enabled.

A similar issue exists for `MAX_THREAD_BYTES`, but its definition in `arch/Kconfig` was not provided, so only the fix for `BOUNDS_CHECK_BYPASS_MITIGATION` can be provided.

The fix is to move the `BOUNDS_CHECK_BYPASS_MITIGATION` Kconfig definition out of the `if USERSPACE` block in `kernel/userspace/Kconfig`.

kernel/userspace/Kconfig
<<<<<<<< SEARCH
config BOUNDS_CHECK_BYPASS_MITIGATION
	bool "Bounds check bypass mitigations for speculative execution"
	help
	  Untrusted parameters from user mode may be used in system calls to
	  index arrays during speculative execution, also known as the Spectre
	  V1 vulnerability. When enabled, various macros defined in
	  misc/speculation.h will insert fence instructions or other appropriate
	  mitigations after bounds checking any array index parameters passed
	  in from untrusted sources (user mode threads). When disabled, these
	  macros do nothing.


rsource "Kconfig.mem_domain"
endif
========
rsource "Kconfig.mem_domain"
endif

config BOUNDS_CHECK_BYPASS_MITIGATION
	bool "Bounds check bypass mitigations for speculative execution"
	help
	  Untrusted parameters from user mode may be used in system calls to
	  index arrays during speculative execution, also known as the Spectre
	  V1 vulnerability. When enabled, various macros defined in
	  misc/speculation.h will insert fence instructions or other appropriate
	  mitigations after bounds checking any array index parameters passed
	  in from untrusted sources (user mode threads). When disabled, these
	  macros do nothing.
>>>>>>>> REPLACE
